sample.selection: First 100 Batch 1 records with status NOINDEX and a same-country/geographic-level near-duplicate match, in batch order.

comparisonMethod.before: Batch 1 recorded 20 stratified peer comparisons per generated page; the fixed test also reconstructs its former composition and recomputes before/after scores against the same tested peer groups.
comparisonMethod.after: Each tested page is compared to every other generated page in the same country and geographic-level group. The visible text array is shared by the registry JSX renderer and evaluator; the unchanged 80% token-Jaccard threshold is applied to that complete page-specific visible text, with no place-name normalization.
comparisonMethod.exactDuplicate: At least one same-group comparison has the same fingerprint after location names are normalized.
comparisonMethod.nearDuplicate: A page is near-duplicate when its maximum same-group normalized similarity is at least 80%.
comparisonMethod.indexability: Existing current page engine result, with any same-test differentiation failure, near-duplicate or exact-duplicate candidate forced to NOINDEX; thresholds are unchanged.

evidenceTierPolicy.STRONG: May proceed to current quality, differentiation, explicit production-approval and sitemap gates; evidence tier alone never makes a route indexable.
evidenceTierPolicy.MEDIUM: Renderable and supported where existing service policy allows; always NOINDEX and excluded from the sitemap.
evidenceTierPolicy.THIN: Renderable with factual geography, regulator guidance and evidence limitations only; always NOINDEX and excluded from the sitemap.

causes: The fixed cohort has mostly THIN evidence profiles, so many pages share the same country regulator, no-evidence status and cautious applicant guidance.
Location hierarchy differs primarily by genuine place names and record type; where same-type records have no distinct sourced aviation facts, the available content cannot support deeper differences.
The existing normalized exact-duplicate metric intentionally removes hierarchy place names, so it exposes pages whose non-name evidence and guidance are identical.

improvement.interpretation: The current page model uses the same visible-text array for JSX rendering and full-page evaluation. The legacy body is reconstructed from the old content engine because the previous JSX renderer is no longer active; treat before/after similarity as a controlled content-model comparison, not archived browser-rendered HTML.

tiers.STRONG: Score >= 70 and requires a verified regulator, sourced hierarchy, at least one primary-source listed pilot-training organization record, a linked FAQ about that training evidence, at least two non-medical evidence records, two non-medical evidence types and two source URLs.
tiers.MEDIUM: Score >= 35 with some primary-source aviation context; renderable, normally NOINDEX pending quality and differentiation. Airports and medical records alone do not establish local pilot training.
tiers.THIN: Lower score or only geography/regulator/generic pathway/unverified gazetteer references; renderable but NOINDEX.

Flight training is a separate stage from classroom or online ground preparation. We One Aviation arranges it with partner flying schools; flying takes place at the selected school.
